findings.text: The [cn_pole_moment] row records the H200 reference JVP/primal ratio as 9.76 (repeated in prose at line 108), but logs/h200-tangents.log:373-375 gives the primal median 0.244 s and the JVP median 2.318 s, a ratio of 9.50, and no line of any log prints 9.76. The conclusion the number supports — that the bound of three sits below what the reference derivative costs — survives at 9.50, so this is a wrong stated value rather than a wrong class.

The mechanism paragraph says the H200 primal compiles in '0.111 to 0.272 s', but the four failing rows' H200 primal medians at logs/h200-tangents.log:331, 352, 373 and 394 are 0.244, 0.111, 0.244 and 0.265 s; 0.272 appears only as one raw sample of the CPU [finite_part] tangent at logs/cpu-elliptic-compile-rows.log:10, so the upper bound is taken from the wrong arm.

The paragraph says the base log 'stopped after 25 of its 28 tests', but the progress line it quotes two lines later is .....................F.F, which is 24 characters (r-20261027T024706009820-moment-field-hessian/suite-files/base/tests__biot__test_elliptic_tangent_recurrences.log:2, measured len=24), and the fragment's own introduction at line 9 states 24 of 28. The same file now carries two different counts.

The sentence says the compile rows at collection positions 20, 21, 23 and 25 'passed there on the CPU at f1e09f09d', but the cited progress line ends at position 24, so position 25 ([harmonic_pole_moments_mirrored]) was never run in that base arm and its outcome cannot be read from the log; only positions 20, 21 and 23 carry a completed progress character.
